title: Reconcile abrupt client disconnects: stream metadata pruning and partial-generation reclamation
creator: Marco Alvarez
description:
Summary:
We need to harden the streaming path to correctly detect client disconnects and timeouts, reclaim transient resources (token buffers, per-request KV cache state, generation contexts), and produce deterministic partial outputs for use in debugging and tool-calling fallbacks. Root cause for recent incidents: stale stream metadata and orphaned generation contexts left open for minutes when clients disconnected mid-token, causing resource pressure and incorrect metrics.

Goals:
- Ensure rapid detection of client disconnects across HTTP/HTTP2/websocket/GRPC clients (including older SDKs that may not send explicit close).
- Reclaim per-request resources (temporary KV cache entries, prefix cache reservations, in-memory token buffers) within a bounded window (configurable, default 5s after disconnect).
- Emit a standardized partial-output artifact when a generation terminates early (schema for structured outputs + tool-calling hints).
- Maintain compatibility with the legacy streaming protocol used by v0.x SDKs; degrade gracefully to a non-streaming response when required.
- Provide observability: metrics, traces, and an incident dashboard for orphaned-context count, reclaim latency, and customer error surface.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Detection: use a three-tier approach: (1) transport-level close notification where available (HTTP/2 RST, websocket close, gRPC CANCEL), (2) idle timeout on request read/write for cases where transport notifications are absent, (3) heartbeat ping from SDKs (optional) to allow faster detection. Trade-off: heartbeats increase client complexity but reduce resource hold time for flaky networks.
- Reclamation window: immediate reclamation risks discarding legitimate long-poll clients; long windows waste memory. Default 5s chosen after load tests; make configurable via runtime-flag and per-customer override on Dedicated.
- Partial outputs: produce a compact artifact with fields (partial_text, last_complete_json, token_count, truncated_reason, request_id, model_version). For structured-output generation (JSON schema outputs) we will attempt a best-effort parse of the last flushed JSON block and include parse_error if invalid. Trade-off: best-effort parsing may surface false positives; include parse_error details to help customers.
- KV cache cleanup: do not immediately evict shared KV cache entries; instead revoke per-request prefixes and add a short tombstone to prevent immediate reuse for different requests. This avoids cross-request contamination at the cost of slightly increased memory footprint for the reclamation window.
- Tool/function calling: if a tool call was in-flight when the client disconnected, mark the tool invocation as orphaned and emit a tool-call-hint in the partial artifact so that higher-level LLM orchestrators (or the customer) can re-run/compensate.

Implementation plan:
1) Instrumentation + detection (Spike, 3d): add transport hooks that normalize disconnect events into a single DisconnectEvent type. Add unit tests that simulate missing transport close but eventual idle timeouts.
2) Resource manager (5d): implement per-request ResourceLease which tracks buffers, KV prefixes, and streaming buffers. ResourceLease supports revoke() and schedules a reclaim timer on disconnect.
3) Partial artifact generator (4d): component that composes partial outputs and best-effort JSON/struct parsing. Add API-level schema and ensure the console can display partials.
4) Backwards compatibility layer (4d): when compatibility header X-Redwood-Stream: legacy is present, follow the legacy flush semantics but still record disconnect events and emit partial artifact as an out-of-band event.
5) Observability + dashboards (3d): Prometheus metrics (orphaned_contexts_total, reclaim_latency_seconds bucketed, partials_emitted_total), tracing spans, and Grafana dashboard.
6) QA / chaos testing (3d): run proxy-level chaos tests that drop connections at random offsets and validate reclamation and correctness.

Acceptance criteria:
- Orphaned contexts do not exceed 5% of peak concurrency under the new reclaim window in load tests.
- Mean reclaim latency < 2s (config default 5s yields reclaim within 2x in 95th percentile).
- Partial artifact schema validated in console and a sample customer flow reproducing a mid-generation disconnect shows tool-call-hint present.
- No regression in streaming latency for healthy clients (<=1% p95 increase).

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag behind runtime flag: streaming.reclaim.enabled (default off for first canary).
- Canary on internal dev org (2% traffic) -> Dedicated staging -> 10% hosted -> 100%. Monitor reclaim_latency and orphaned_contexts.

Open questions:
- Should tombstones for KV prefixes be configurable by model class (some large-context models may need longer retention)?
- SDK heartbeat: should we require it in the next major SDK release or keep optional?

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence: /confluence/redwood/streaming-disconnects-design (draft)
- GitHub PR (WIP): github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842
- Incident runbook entry: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ops/pages/STREAM-INCIDENT-2026

Migration notes for customers:
- For customers using function/tool calling, we will include an optional header X-Redwood-Partial-Artifact: true to receive partial artifacts as a separate event post-disconnect. Older SDKs will receive partials embedded as final flush frames where supported.

Security & compliance:
- Partial artifacts may include generated text and tool-call metadata. Ensure the artifact respects data-retention rules; we'll copy artifacts only to ephemeral traces and a short-term store (90d max) unless customer opts in for longer retention.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Spike instrumentation and ResourceLease prototype (Anika) -> PR for review.
- Draft partial artifact schema and console adapter (Jeff, PM pairing).
- Add canary rollout plan to release playbook and get SRE sign-off.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Marco Alvarez: Created ticket after postmortem for STREAM-2026-02. Noted cross-team dependencies with Console and SDKs.

2026-02-20 - Anika Shah: Completed detection spike. Found that some websocket clients never send a close frame; relied on idle timeouts that were set too high (60s). Proposed default idle timeout 5s for streaming sockets.

2026-02-24 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Reviewed proposed reclaim behavior; asked for metrics around memory freed per reclaim to validate resource benefit. Requested canary throttles for Dedicated customers.

2026-02-28 - Design review (Priya Menon): Console partial artifact UI proposed: toast with 'partial generation available' and a link to view structured artifact. Need to avoid spamming customers for frequent partials.

2026-03-05 - Anika Shah: ResourceLease prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842. Added unit tests for revoke() semantics. Needs review from infra team for concurrency model.
